title: Polynomial time bound implies polynomial nondeterministic time
statement: Let $L$ be a language of binary strings and let $C,c\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose there are natural numbers $K,r$ and a finite nondeterministic Turing machine that decides $L$ within time $K\bigl(n+C(n+1)^c+1\bigr)^r$. Then $L$ belongs to $\bigcup_{e\in\mathbb{N}}\mathrm{NTIME}(n^e+1)$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language of binary strings
There exist $K,r\in\mathbb{N}$ and a finite nondeterministic machine deciding $L$ within the stated time bound
replaced: Let $L$ be a language over the binary alphabet and $C, c$ natural numbers. If some nondeterministic machine decides $L$ within time $K\,(n + C(n+1)^c + 1)^r$ for some constants $K$ and $r$, then $L$ belongs to $\bigcup_{e} \mathrm{NTIME}(n^e + 1)$.
